references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew where the Sadducees ask Jesus the same question: "In the resurrection, whose wife will she be of the seven?" ([ref:Matt 22:28|Matthew 22:28]).
The parallel passage in Mark where the same question is asked: "Whose wife will she be among them in the resurrection?" ([ref:Mark 12:23|Mark 12:23]).

The background to the question is levirate marriage (the duty of a brother-in-law), where a man was to marry his deceased brother's widow to raise up offspring for him ([ref:5 Mos 25:5-6|Deuteronomy 25:5-6]).

The context of the question: the Sadducees, who deny the resurrection, come to Jesus with this hypothetical scenario in an attempt to make the doctrine of the resurrection look absurd ([ref:Luk 20:27|Luke 20:27]).

Jesus' answer to the question: In the resurrection people neither marry nor are given in marriage, for they can no longer die, but are like angels and are children of God by being children of the resurrection ([ref:Luk 20:34-36|Luke 20:34-36]).

Paul's teaching on the different nature of the resurrection body – the natural body is sown in perishability but raised in imperishability – emphasizes that life after the resurrection is fundamentally different from our present existence ([ref:1 Kor 15:42-44|1 Corinthians 15:42-44]).
